per_question.question: What medical loss ratio (MLR) must Medicaid managed care organizations meet under federal law, and how does NC implement this requirement?
per_question.agent_answer:
Under federal law, Medicaid managed care plans do **not automatically have a universal federal minimum MLR they must meet**. Instead, federal law requires states to make each MCO/PIHP/PAHP **calculate and report** its MLR, and **if** a state chooses to impose a minimum MLR, that state-set minimum must be **at least 85%**. North Carolina goes further: its managed care contract sets a **minimum MLR threshold of 88% in aggregate across all contracted PHPs**, with each PHP’s threshold calculated based on its capitation revenue mix. [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)] [[Contract--30-190029-DHB-Prepaid-Health-Plan-Services RFP](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-190029-dhb-prepaid-health-plan-services-rfp/download?attachment)]

## Federal rule

### 1) What federal law requires
For contracts starting on or after July 1, 2017, the state must ensure that each Medicaid MCO, PIHP, and PAHP **calculates and reports** an MLR under the federal methodology. [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]

### 2) Minimum threshold under federal law
Federal law says:

- **If a state elects to mandate a minimum MLR**, that minimum must be **equal to or higher than 85%**. [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]
- So **85% is the federal floor for any state-imposed minimum**, not a standalone nationwide minimum automatically imposed by the regulation itself. [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]

### 3) How the federal MLR is calculated
Federal law defines MLR as the ratio of:

- **Numerator**: incurred claims + expenditures for activities that improve health care quality + fraud prevention activities. [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]
- **Denominator**: adjusted premium revenue, with taxes and licensing/regulatory fees treated under the federal denominator rules. [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]

The federal regulation also specifies key inclusions/exclusions, including:

- incurred claims include direct provider claims, unpaid claim liabilities, certain withholds, reserve changes, and some provider incentive/bonus payments tied to defined clinical or quality standards; [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]
- incurred claims must deduct overpayment recoveries and prescription drug rebates; and [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]
- non-claims administrative costs are excluded. [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]

A plan’s MLR may also be adjusted through a **credibility adjustment** under the federal rule. [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]

### 4) Federal reporting and remittance oversight
If a state uses a minimum MLR requirement, the state must annually report to CMS, for each plan, at least:

- numerator amount,
- denominator amount,
- MLR percentage,
- member months, and
- any remittances owed. [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]

And if the state requires remittances for failing to meet the state’s minimum MLR, the state must reimburse CMS for the federal share of the remittance. [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]

## North Carolina implementation

North Carolina implements the federal requirement in its PHP contract by requiring annual MLR calculation and reporting on **two bases**:

1. a **CMS-defined MLR** under 42 C.F.R. § 438.8; and  
2. a **Department-defined MLR** with North Carolina-specific adjustments. [[Contract--30-190029-DHB-Prepaid-Health-Plan-Services RFP](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-190029-dhb-prepaid-health-plan-services-rfp/download?attachment)]

### 1) CMS-defined MLR in NC
The contract tracks the federal framework:

- numerator = incurred claims + expenditures for activities that improve health care quality + the lesser of fraud reduction expenditures or fraud reduction recoveries; [[Contract--30-190029-DHB-Prepaid-Health-Plan-Services RFP](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-190029-dhb-prepaid-health-plan-services-rfp/download?attachment)]
- denominator = premium revenue minus federal, state, and local taxes and licensing/regulatory fees. [[Contract--30-190029-DHB-Prepaid-Health-Plan-Services RFP](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-190029-dhb-prepaid-health-plan-services-rfp/download?attachment)]

### 2) Department-defined MLR in NC
NC then modifies that formula for its own contractual enforcement. The contract says the Department-defined numerator may include certain **voluntary contributions to health-related resources** that align with the Department’s Quality Strategy and meet specified community-engagement and beneficiary-outcome conditions. [[Contract--30-190029-DHB-Prepaid-Health-Plan-Services RFP](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-190029-dhb-prepaid-health-plan-services-rfp/download?attachment)]

But NC excludes certain items from that numerator, including:

- certain required additional directed provider payments reimbursed separately by the Department, and
- payments to related providers that violate contractual payment limitations. [[Contract--30-190029-DHB-Prepaid-Health-Plan-Services RFP](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-190029-dhb-prepaid-health-plan-services-rfp/download?attachment)]

The Department-defined denominator is similarly adjusted to subtract Department reimbursements for certain required additional directed payments, along with associated taxes and fees. [[Contract--30-190029-DHB-Prepaid-Health-Plan-Services RFP](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-190029-dhb-prepaid-health-plan-services-rfp/download?attachment)]

### 3) NC-specific exclusions and adjustments
The NC contract also states that for both CMS-defined and Department-defined MLR:

- the Department reviews and approves the PHP’s classification of quality-improvement activities;
- the numerator must exclude, among other things, interest or penalty payments for prompt-pay failures;
- the numerator must exclude non-claims costs under 42 C.F.R. § 438.8(e)(2)(v)(A), PBM fees and spread pricing, marketing/branding material, related-party administrative payments and margin, and administrative costs not allowed as HCQI, including corporate allocations; and
- plans with fewer than **380,000 member months** must use a credibility adjustment as defined in 42 C.F.R. § 438.8(h)(1)-(3). [[Contract--30-190029-DHB-Prepaid-Health-Plan-Services RFP](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-190029-dhb-prepaid-health-plan-services-rfp/download?attachment)]

### 4) NC’s minimum threshold and consequence
North Carolina’s contract states:

- the **minimum MLR threshold in aggregate across all contracted PHPs shall be exactly 88%**; and
- if a PHP’s **Department-defined MLR** is below the minimum threshold, the PHP must either:
  - remit a rebate to the Department,
  - make approved contributions to health-related resources, or
  - split the obligation between the two. [[Contract--30-190029-DHB-Prepaid-Health-Plan-Services RFP](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-190029-dhb-prepaid-health-plan-services-rfp/download?attachment)]

## Bottom line

- **Federal law:** states must require Medicaid managed care plans to **calculate and report** MLR; if a state imposes a minimum, it must be **at least 85%**. [[42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)]
- **North Carolina:** NC contractually implements that framework and sets a stricter **88% minimum MLR threshold in aggregate across contracted PHPs**, enforced through rebates and/or approved health-related resource contributions when a PHP’s Department-defined MLR falls short. [[Contract--30-190029-DHB-Prepaid-Health-Plan-Services RFP](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-190029-dhb-prepaid-health-plan-services-rfp/download?attachment)]
